name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3267
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email January 9, 2013 This article appears in the January 28, 2013 issue.

clue.text: I deal with last vestige of power blackout externally in theatrical offering

indicators.note: something placed externally sits on the outside, so the word for blackout wraps around the rest
last points to the closing letter of the phrase after it

blocks.note: a coma is a deep loss of consciousness
taken as written
to cope is to deal with something
the final letter of power

explanation.surface: A stage show staged in the dark after a power cut, with the speaker coping with the outage.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackout reads as a power cut, matching the surface, but here it means losing consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic opera is a light, humorous stage work with music, a kind of show put on in a theatre.

clue.text: Memorable cold front wrecked yacht

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
something wrecked is smashed apart, so these letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of cold
the five letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: An unforgettable storm system sinks a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold front' reads as weather, but front acts only on cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune is one that sticks in the mind, easily remembered.

clue.text: Lying to improve a metropolis

blocks.note: to mend is to fix or improve
taken as written
a metropolis is a large city

explanation.surface: Telling fibs in order to make a big city look better.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying is the noun here, the habit of telling untruths, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is untruthfulness, the act or habit of telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Drag irritated Italian or Russian

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
Italian and Russian are both kinds of salad dressing

explanation.surface: A tedious, annoyed person from Italy or Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Italian and Russian look like nationalities but are salad dressings. Drag is the noun for wearing the other sex's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing in drag means dressing in clothing of the opposite sex, which is exactly that practice.

clue.text: Chanteuse embraces Brel's final entrée

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the singer's name wraps around the other letter
final points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Edith Piaf, the great French chanteuse
the closing letter of Brel

explanation.surface: A French singer hugs Jacques Brel as his last number begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage an entrée is the main course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaf is a rice dish cooked in stock, served as a main course.

clue.text: No-goodnik mother in Dutch port

blocks.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A villain's mother living in a harbour town in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother in' looks like a container signal; here in just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major seaport city of the Netherlands, among Europe's largest harbours.

clue.text: Support a wager

blocks.note: taken as written
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to back a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so it is a verb of backing.

clue.text: Forehead on Northern California politician

blocks.note: the brow is the forehead
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Something lands on the brow of a lawmaker from the north of the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern looks like part of 'Northern California' but only supplies N; Jerry Brown was California's governor when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry Brown, governor of California, is a famous politician from that state with this surname.

clue.text: Caddy instructs leader of trainees

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to instruct is to teach
the opening letter of trainees

explanation.surface: A golf caddy coaches the first of the beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: Caddy looks like the golfer's helper, but it means a tea caddy, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a box for storing tea, and a tea chest is a larger such container.

clue.text: Work around broken fin's metal sheeting

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of their proper order, so these letters are rearranged
around means one word encloses the other, here the word for work on the outside

blocks.note: to toil is to work hard
the three letters of fin, shuffled

explanation.surface: A repair job on a damaged fin uses sheets of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The container splits the word for work after its first letter rather than wrapping it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal rolled into a sheet, used in kitchens for wrapping food.

clue.text: Bizarrely, I coat Pa with pudding

indicators.note: bizarrely says the following letters come out in a strange, unexpected arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An odd scene of someone smearing their father with dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starch from cassava, commonly cooked with milk into a sweet milky dessert.

clue.text: Talking chicken gets unexpected recognition

indicators.note: talking means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: a pullet is a young hen
a surprise is something unexpected

explanation.surface: A speaking hen wins sudden fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Pullet surprise, a young hen plus something unexpected, sounds like the famous American award, a classic pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pulitzer is a prestigious American award honouring journalism, literature and music, a mark of acclaim.

clue.text: Difficult phase for many

indicators.note: difficult suggests a word that is awkward or troublesome, so its letters are worked into another order

blocks.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rough patch that a lot of people go through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult phase' reads as one idea, like a troubled spell, but difficult is the signal acting on phase.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps is an informal word for a large quantity, as in heaps of friends, so it stands for lots.

clue.text: Dance in good-time church? Supposedly, there's no such thing

indicators.note: in places the dance word inside the word for good time

blocks.note: fun is a good time
a reel is a lively Scottish or Irish dance
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Dancing in a lively, fun-loving church sounds too good to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'There's no such thing as a free lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says nothing comes truly free, so a meal at no cost is the thing said not to exist.

clue.text: Fighter plane assessed and moved to another country

blocks.note: the MiG is a Soviet-designed fighter jet
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: A warplane was evaluated and then relocated abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to relocate from one land or region to another, as people or birds do.

clue.text: Bring up illustration that dominates European nation lacking new brand

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means reading the word from bottom to top
lacking means without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: art is a picture or illustration
a Scandinavian country
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Raise a picture of something ruling over a European land without a new logo.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'dominates' simply means the reversed piece sits on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a registered name or symbol identifying a company's goods, which is what a brand is.

clue.text: In retrospect, clean up the beginning of swift currents

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word for clean up is read from its end
the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: to edit a text is to clean it up
the opening letter of swift

explanation.surface: Looking back, someone cleans up the start of fast-moving water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, and the flows of water they produce are currents.

clue.text: Unusual birthday featuring musical opening and short poem

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an irregular new order
an opening is a beginning, so just the first letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
the opening letter of musical

explanation.surface: An odd birthday party with a musical number and a little verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Merriam-Webster defines a dithyramb as a usually short poem in an inspired wild irregular strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb began as an ancient Greek choral hymn to Dionysus and now names any wild, rapturous verse.

clue.text: Horse I'd almost race backwards in a sweater

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
backwards says the whole string is read from its end

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse
taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone would nearly ride a horse in reverse while wearing a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: RACE loses its E, then NAG, ID and RAC are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted top that buttons down the front, one kind of sweater.

clue.text: A shortstop buried near a hole

indicators.note: something buried is put inside, so the word for near goes within the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
by means beside or near
SS is the scorecard abbreviation for the baseball position shortstop

explanation.surface: A baseball infielder lies buried beside a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: BY sits between A and SS. A shortstop plays between second and third base in baseball, abbreviated SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a deep chasm, a seemingly bottomless hole in the ground.

clue.text: What some chairs have: collars restricting movement at first

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the collars word closes around the other letter
at first points to the opening letter alone

blocks.note: to collar a suspect is slang for arresting them
the opening letter of movement

explanation.surface: Chairs fitted with restraining collars that stop anyone moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Collar, as a verb, is police slang for catching a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Armrests are the side supports on which a seated person lays their forearms, fitted to many chairs.

clue.text: Trunk with weapon that could be a companion to a mighty hammer?

blocks.clueFragment: that could be a companion to a mighty hammer?
blocks.note: the Norse god of thunder wields the mighty hammer Mjolnir
ax is the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: A tree trunk alongside an axe, fit to pair with a great hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk looks like a tree or a box but means the torso; the god owns the hammer, so he is its companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest, the part of the body between neck and abdomen, also called the trunk.

clue.text: Quality of twilight: sun-kissed, phantasmagorical

indicators.note: phantasmagorical describes shifting, dreamlike images, so the letters before it are transformed into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dreamy description of an evening sky glowing from the setting sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim light at the end of day, so duskiness is that gloomy state.

clue.text: Yell, "Be quiet! Scram!"

blocks.note: sh is the hushing call
Out! orders someone to leave

explanation.surface: Someone bellows orders to be silent and get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout is to call out loudly, the same as to holler.

clue.text: It is suppressed by trespass and direct action

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a trespass is a sin, as in the Lord's Prayer

explanation.surface: A protest is stifled by trespassing laws and by protesters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave, a form of direct action.

clue.text: Essential aspect of narcolepsy challenges the science of behavior, briefly

indicators.note: an essential aspect lies at the core, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of narcolepsy and the start of challenges

explanation.surface: A sleep disorder's central feature puzzles psychologists.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says a key symptom of narcolepsy baffles researchers; the answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Psych is a short informal form of psychology, the study of mind and behaviour.

clue.text: Former Soviet republic that would be sweet with 7?

blocks.note: a country once part of the USSR
joined to the answer at 7 Down it names the jazz standard Sweet ___ ___

explanation.walkthrough: 7 Down is BROWN, and the song is Sweet Georgia Brown, so the republic must share its name with the song's girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia, in the Caucasus, was one of the fifteen Soviet republics until independence in 1991.

clue.text: Deceptive hint: song, or where it might disappear

indicators.note: deceptive means not what it seems, so the letters following are disguised in a new order

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A misleading clue lies in a song's lyrics, or in where the song fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: Things are said to vanish into thin air, which is the fair link to 'where it might disappear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'vanish into thin air' makes thin air the place where something goes missing.

clue.text: Lunatics stagger back

indicators.note: back says the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: to stagger someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Mad people reel backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for crazy people, as in a nut, an eccentric or madman.

clue.text: Hide Ecstasy in Bronx bughouse — it's useful for distributing rewards and punishments

definitions.text: it's useful for distributing rewards and punishments

indicators.note: bughouse is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: a hide is an animal's skin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hides a drug in a madhouse in the Bronx.
explanation.walkthrough: Bughouse looks like a noun meaning asylum, but as slang for crazy it is the anagram signal on E plus BRONX.
explanation.definitionFit: B. F. Skinner's operant conditioning chamber trains animals by delivering food rewards or shocks.
